decisions.reason: The candidate already has a separate same-message MODIFY for sanitation, liquid traps, and removable cleaning components; the food-contact material standard adds no further cleanability-state change.
Requiring food-safe contact materials does not change the bowl capacity, depth, size, or form requirements.
The bowls were already required to be easy to remove and swap; the new material standard does not change that removal behavior or clearance.
The selected whisk is already stainless steel, and the broader food-safe material standard does not change its head style, size, positioning, or material selection.
The food-contact material standard constrains material suitability but does not necessarily alter the off-the-shelf electronic strategy or the existing custom stainless-steel spout strategy.
Food-contact material requirements do not change the input power source, power-supply capacity, controller capacity, or electrical load margin.
The source establishes a food-contact material standard but does not require an immediate BOM revision; the longer-term documentation suggestion is explicitly not required now.
The material standard applies to food-contact areas and does not change the accepted enclosure bulk, bowl-well accommodation, or overall form.
Food-safe material selection does not change the required flow profile, dispensing sequence, froth preservation, or sputtering constraint.
The food-contact material standard does not modify the required smoothness, foam quality, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The source material decision does not change the splash-control target, accepted control methods, or high-speed splash behavior.
Food-contact material suitability does not change the event-use reliability or electrical load-capacity requirements.
